payload.headline: Netflix reaches the first buy zone; start small, add only at 58.03

summary.thesis: Netflix is a grade B business priced near the bottom of its own history, but slower sales growth, peak margins and falling estimates mean the price may not have found a floor yet.
summary.decision: Long-term: buy a small first position at 59.68 and add at 58.03. Swing: no trade while the stock trends down below its falling averages.
summary.act_at: Buy small at 59.68, add at 58.03, no buying above 62.64

payload.happening: Netflix closed at 59.82, up 0.23% on the day. It is still in a downtrend, below its falling 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (63.17, 68.17 and 80.17), and our data lists no support level below the price. The only news is a confirmed season 2 trailer for 3 Body Problem. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-19.
payload.business: Nothing today changes the business. The 3 Body Problem trailer affects mood only. New shows keep members engaged (general knowledge), but the trailer moves no number here. The business itself is still solid. Revenue over the last 12 months (TTM) was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, rose to 11.4B from 9.0B. Operating margin, the profit kept from each dollar of sales before interest and tax, rose to 31.3% from 29.14%. The share count fell 3.35% over the year, so each share owns more of the company. Two things are at risk. The first is growth: sales grew 11.85% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, down from 16.19% two quarters before. The second is margins: the filings note that 31% is the top of the 5-year range of 17–31%, and peaks like this usually fade. Analysts are also trimming forecasts. This quarter's earnings-per-share estimate fell 7.3% in 30 days. Cash is not at risk: free cash flow of 11.4B is large next to net debt of 4.4B (debt of 12.7B against cash of 8.2B). Segment data is not available, so we cannot say which regions or products are slowing.

worth.text: At 59.82 the stock trades at 17.0 times trailing earnings and 15.9 times next year's expected earnings. On sales, it trades at 4.9 times, below the 7.0 median of its large-tech peers and at the 20th percentile of its own 5-year history. A discounted cash flow model (DCF) values a company by adding up its future cash, discounted back to today. Here it gives 37.01 (bear), 62.64 (base) and 74.6 (bull). The stock's own price-to-sales history gives 59.68, 84.5 and 122.15. The price implies free cash flow growth starting at 13.4% a year. Growth is the assumption that drives the gap. Starting at 10%, the stock is worth 52.14. Starting at 20%, it is worth 77.74. Margins matter almost as much. If operating margin falls to 23%, value drops to 58.03. At 15%, it drops to 38.33. The own-history values are higher because they assume investors pay the multiples of past years, when growth was faster. The price sits near fair value, not far below it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing between 10% and 20% a year, close to the 13.4% the price implies, even though quarterly sales growth has slowed to 11.85%.

bull: Cash generation is rising: trailing free cash flow reached 11.4B, up from 9.0B a year earlier.
The stock is cheap against peers and its own past: price-to-sales of 4.9 against a peer median of 7.0, at the 20th percentile of its 5-year range.
Profitability is improving and buybacks are shrinking the share count: operating margin is 31.3%, up from 29.14%, and shares fell 3.35% over the year.
bear: Growth is slowing: quarterly sales growth fell to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters earlier, and the filings flag that sales growth is slowing.
Margins sit at a 5-year peak of 31%; if operating margin fades to 23%, value is 58.03, and at 15% it is 38.33.
Estimates are falling and the chart is weak: this quarter's EPS estimate was cut 7.3% in 30 days, and the price is below the 200-day average of 80.17 with no support level listed.

levels.what: Low end of the own-history price-to-sales range, next to the 60 put strike with the most open interest (39724). This is the level for a first, small position.
Value if operating margin fades to 23%. At this price the margin-peak risk is already in the price, so this is where to add.
DCF base value. Above it, the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: A grade B business is now trading at the low end of its own valuation history and below the DCF base of 62.64. Estimates are still being cut and no support is listed, so the position starts small and grows only at lower prices.

swing.why: The trend is down: lower highs and lower lows, below the falling 20-day average of 63.17, with resistance at 61.15–61.63 and 64.56–65.08 and no support below. No trade until the stock closes above 63.17 and the 64.56–65.08 zone.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report comes before the 2027-02-19 option expiry, and options price a move of about 17.0% by then, so buying before the report stays at the small first position and any add waits for 58.03 or a report that holds margin near 31.3%.

change_mind: If the 2027-01-19 report shows quarterly sales growth below 11.85% and operating margin below 29.14%, the plan changes from buy to wait and the add level drops toward the 52.14 value.
If next-year EPS estimates fall below the current low of 3.56, falling estimates are eroding the valuation case, so further buying stops.
A close above the 20-day average of 63.17 and the 64.56–65.08 resistance would end the lower-highs pattern and turn the swing view from no trade to enter.
payload.what_changed: Changed: from wait to buy (small), because the price fell to 59.82, below the 60.37 first-buy level set in the last note and right at the new low end of the own-history range (59.68).
payload.label: Research, not advice.
